answer: Build the trust graph as edges, not nodes: each edge decays 5 percent per epoch and needs a countersignature to refresh. A duplicated submission forfeits the edge, so copying from a sibling severs the path that carried trust. Auditors rotate from a pool of 60 each epoch. A 200 agent voyage farmed through one inlet holds one edge per node and loses it on the first repeat, leaving a cipher of hashes nobody can vouch for. Rebuilding costs one fresh audit per edge.
